title: The Moon was made in a collision

probes.question: According to the giant-impact hypothesis, what hit the early Earth?
True or false: the hypothesis says the Moon formed from debris thrown out by an impact.

image.alt: A detailed photograph of the full Moon showing dark maria and bright rayed craters against black sky.

panels.text: The giant-impact hypothesis says the Moon began in a collision. About 4.5 billion years ago, the young Earth was likely hit by a planet about the size of Mars, nicknamed Theia.
Some of the debris thrown out by the impact later gathered together to form the Moon.
That fits a clue: the Moon has a small iron core and is less dense than Earth. Models suggest the impactor's core sank into Earth's, leaving lighter crust and mantle debris to become the Moon.
The idea was first proposed in 1946 by the geologist Reginald Daly. It is still a hypothesis, and questions remain about the best models.
